name: Laryngotracheoesophageal Cleft Type 1

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Endoscopic Diagnostic Criteria for Laryngotracheoesophageal Cleft

criteria.description: Direct endoscopic visualization of a cleft extending from the interarytenoid region into the posterior larynx without involvement of the trachea
Presence of feeding difficulties with aspiration and recurrent respiratory infections in neonates or infants
Contrast esophagography demonstrating contrast passage into the airway through the cleft

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Endoscopic visualization of the cleft plus clinical presentation consistent with aspiration or feeding difficulties
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and endoscopic; imaging supports but is not definitive alone.

searchTerms: cleft between vocal cords seen on scope
gap between arytenoid cartilages on laryngoscopy

pathognomonic.symptomName: Aspiration of food or liquids during swallowing
searchTerms: food or drink going into airway
recurrent pneumonia due to inhaled food or liquids

occasional.symptomName: Failure to thrive due to feeding intolerance
searchTerms: failure to gain weight due to feeding issues

rare.symptomName: Pulmonary hypertension secondary to chronic aspiration
searchTerms: high blood pressure in lungs from aspiration
lung hypertension due to inhaled food

rare.symptomName: Neurological impairment due to hypoxic episodes
searchTerms: nerve impairment due to oxygen loss

laboratory: Elevated inflammatory markers during aspiration pneumonia episodes
Possible hypoxemia on arterial blood gas during respiratory distress
imaging: Contrast esophagography showing contrast leakage into airway
Chest X-ray demonstrating recurrent infiltrates consistent with aspiration pneumonia
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; may be associated with syndromes involving midline defects

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of fistulous connection between trachea and esophagus usually distal
More severe respiratory distress at birth
Membranous tissue partially obstructing the laryngeal inlet
No communication between esophagus and airway

redFlags: Severe aspiration pneumonia refractory to treatment
Failure to thrive due to feeding difficulties
Apnea or cyanotic episodes during feeding
references: Kamel MH, et al. Laryngeal clefts: diagnosis and management. Int J Pediatr Otorhinolaryngol. 2017.
Holinger LD. Laryngeal clefts: a review. Ann Otol Rhinol Laryngol. 1989.
